nodes.summary: MULTIWAY NUMBER PARTITION is the decision problem on bitstrings that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a multiway number partition instance $(a, K)$ that is feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to a multiway number partition instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The MULTIWAY NUMBER PARTITION decision problem

nodes.summary: Let $(a, K)$ be a multiway number partition instance with $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{m-1})$. It is feasible when $K \ge 1$ and there is a map $f$ from $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ onto $\{0, \dots, K-1\}$ such that the sums $\sum_{j < m,\, f(j) = p} a_j$ for $p = 0, \dots, K-1$ are all equal. In other words, the entries of $a$, counted with repetition, can be split into $K$ nonempty parts with equal sums.
nodes.title: Feasible multiway number partition instances

nodes.summary: A multiway number partition instance is a pair $(a, K)$ consisting of a list $a$ of natural numbers and a natural number $K$ (the number of parts).
nodes.title: Multiway number partition instances

nodes.summary: Let MULTIWAY NUMBER PARTITION be the decision problem that accepts exactly the bitstrings decoding to a feasible multiway number partition instance: a list of natural numbers and a number $K \ge 1$ such that the entries of the list, counted with repetition, can be split into $K$ nonempty parts with equal sums.
